newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bond traders now ponder the bottom.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bond traders now ponder the bottom.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures analysts Tuesday were trying to assess how much downside remains to be explored two days after the four-month bull run derailed.
September bond futures have crept sideways to lower since plunging almost two full points on very heavy volume Friday, diminishing expectations for additional followthrough.
"It's still up for grabs," said a bond floor trader.
Technicians and traders said the contract's ability to notch lower lows in coming days will help solve the riddle of whether downside momentum has been largely spent.
"Near-term risk favors a recovery right now through the 114-28/32 to 115-00/32 level to stabilize the recent weakness," said A. Gary Flagler, first vice president at First Chicago Futures Inc.
However, he continued, "the inability to break above 114-28 today and a failure of yesterday's 114-12/32 low would suggest an extention of losses targeting 113-27/32."
A pullback to that area would pave the way for a further decline to 113-00/32 to 112-16/32 this week, Flagler said.
The September futures contract edged to a session low of 114-11 this morning before losses stalled and was last trading down 4/32 at 114-17/32.

Robert Zukowski, senior capital markets technician for Pegasus Econometric Group, predicted this week's quarterly Treasury refunding auctions would press the market toward the low end of an expected trading range spanning roughly 117-00/32 to 113-00/32.
"I don't think Friday's plunge is going to be easily reversed," said the analyst.
Below that range, Zukowski said, support at 112-24/32 would be a critical test for the market. The level represents the 38.2 percent retracement of the move up from the April 11 low of 105-30/32.

But if futures manage to hold in the 114-00 handle, the contract could be headed back up to revisit Friday's breakout point at about 116-00/32, the level where the sell-off accelerated, Zukowski said.
The lack of bearish momentum so far this week suggests such a rebound is possible, he said.
"It has been a slow bleed. We need only a small band-aid to patch up what's going on now," said Zukowski.
"It just doesn't feel like this is a huge trend change here."
